questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Oprah Winfrey is one of the richest and most powerful American women, loved and admired by everyone.

B. When she was only 19, she became the first black female assistant to Nashville’s evening news anchor.

C. But Oprah had a very difficult and traumatic childhood.

D. In 1986, Oprah became the television presenter of her own talk show called ‘The Oprah Winfrey Show’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e., 'ABDC'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly. 
 
• The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 
 
• Here, only A is independent and introduces an American celebrity Oprah Winfrey as the subject of the passage under discussion.
 
• So, A becomes the first sentence of the passage. 
 
• The only option that shows A as the first sentence is option 4.
 
• As per option 4, the full sequence is : ABDC.
 
 
• 
 
**A.** Oprah Winfrey is one of the richest and most powerful American women, loved and admired by everyone.

 
 
• 
 
**B. **When she was only 19, she became the first black female assistant to Nashville’s evening news anchor.

 
 
• 
 
**D.** In 1986, Oprah became the television presenter of her own talk show called ‘The Oprah Winfrey Show’.

 
 
• 
 
**C.** But Oprah had a very difficult and traumatic childhood.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
This sequence is logically correct, making option 4 the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

Every participant gave/ so outstanding performance/ that it became difficult/ to choose the winner.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e., 'so outstanding performance'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error lies with the part **'... so outstanding performance ...' **
 
• **Outstanding performance **is a **noun phrase. **
 
• **So **is an **adverb **that can only be used with **adjectives. **
 
• Hence, the phrase **'... so outstanding performance ...' ** is incorrect. 
 
• The correct word to use here is the **determiner such **followed by the **article an.**

**So the correct sentence is- ***Every participant gave/ **such an outstanding performance**/ that it became difficult/ to choose the winner. *

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with most appropriate word.

I am ______ of joining the armed forces.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e., 'desirous'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given blank needs an **adjective **that goes with the following **preposition of. **
 
• There are no definite rules when it comes to combining adjectives with prepositions, but a few patterns exist.
 
• One such pattern is to memorize the prepositions used with adjectives’ associated noun forms.
 
• Let us look at the noun forms of the given adjectives and the prepositions they associate with - 
 
 
• **desirous - ***noun form → ***desire - ***associated preposition → **of***
 
• eager - *noun form → *eagerness - *associated preposition → *for
 
• keen - *noun form → *keenness - *associated preposition → *with
 
• interested - *noun form → *interest - *associated preposition → *in
 
 
 
• From the above explanation it is clear that **desirous **is the correct word for the given blank.
 
• This makes **option 1 **the correct answer.

• Thus, **to go on **is the correct replacement for the underlined part. 
 
• This makes **option 1 **the correct answer. 

**Hence, the correct sentence is-** The workers’ union has threatened **to go on** an indefinite strike

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

A school teacher earns f__ewer salary from__ a college lecturer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e., 'a lower salary than'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let us analyze the given sentence first.
 
• In the given sentence a comparison is happening between the salary earned by a school teacher and a college lecturer. 
 
• **Salary **in this instance is an **uncountable noun. **
 
• **Fewer **is a **determiner **that is used with **countable nouns.**
 
• So, we need to change **fewer **to **lower. **
 
• We also need to add the **conjunction than **to introduce the **second element in a comparison (a college lecturer).**
 
• Thus, the underlined part should be replaced with **a lower salary than.**
 
• This makes **option 3 **the correct answer. 

**The correct sentence is-** A school teacher earns **a lower salary than** a college lecturer.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

She has put fresh flowers in the flower vase.

options.text: Fresh flowers are put in the flower vase.
Fresh flowers have been put by her in the flower vase.
Fresh flowers are being put in the flower vase.
Fresh flowers has been put in the flower vase.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e., 'Fresh flowers have been put by her in the flower vase.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **present perfect tense (has put)**
 
• It has the following sentence pattern - **Subject **(she) + **has + past participle** (put) + **object** (fresh flowers) + **adjunct** (in the flower vase). 
 
• To change to passive form, we need to use the following sentence pattern - **Original object + has been + past participle + by original subject ****+** adjunct
 
• It should be noted that the **original subject** of the active voice sentence is the **pronoun she.**
 
• In passive voice this changes to her. 
 
• Following the above sentence pattern we get the following sentence - Fresh flowers have been put by her in the flower vase.
 
• This makes option 2 the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given blank needs a superlative adjective form. 
 
• From the given options, it is clear that this form is the **superlative form **of the **adjective lovely. **
 
• Thus, **option 4 **or **loveliest **is the correct word for the given blank. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When we form the degrees of comparison for adjectives, we need to follow certain rules. 
 
• In the given case, **lovely** is the positive that **ends in 'y'** and has a **consonant (L)** before it.
 
• To form the **comparative **and the **superlative, **we **change 'y' into 'i'** and then **add 'er' and 'est' **respectively.
 
• **Lovely → Lovelier → Loveliest**
